blocks.label: PART 1: BIG IDEAS
items: 1. The time scale, largest to smallest: eon → era → period → epoch.
2. Most fossils are found in sedimentary rock.
3. Oxygen built up in the air (the Great Oxidation Event, about 2.4 billion years ago) because photosynthesis released it faster than rocks and iron could absorb it.
4. Rising oxygen made complex, oxygen-using life possible.
5. When volcanoes build up CO₂ in the air, temperatures go up.
6. In the Carboniferous, as CO₂ declined and O₂ rose above modern levels, southern Gondwana glaciated.
7. When ice sheets grow, sea level falls.
8. In the Cambrian, all life lived in the sea; plants, then animals, later moved onto land.
9. Pangaea was fully assembled by the Permian, then began breaking apart in the Late Triassic, opening the Atlantic Ocean.
10. The ends of the Paleozoic and Mesozoic Eras are each marked by a mass extinction.
11. After each of those die-offs, rebuilding ecosystems took millions of years.
12. Since the Mesozoic greenhouse faded, Earth's climate has gradually cooled.
